name: Trinidad
summary: Spanish sovereignty, a British conquest, and a shared national future.
notes: Trinidad and Tobago were not one colonial unit until 1889. Early Spanish settlements repeatedly failed; 1592 marks the enduring colonial capital.

events.title: Spain claims Trinidad
events.detail: Columbus’s third voyage reached the island.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: Indigenous resistance at Cumucurapo
events.detail: Resistance defeated an early Spanish colonizing attempt.

events.title: San José de Oruña founded
events.detail: Antonio de Berrío’s expedition established a durable colonial capital.

events.title: Raleigh raids San José
events.detail: English forces captured the governor and burned the settlement, without establishing lasting rule.

events.title: Trinidad falls to Britain
events.detail: A British fleet and army compelled the Spanish governor to surrender.

events.title: Spain cedes Trinidad
events.detail: The Treaty of Amiens confirmed the British conquest.

events.title: Trinidad and Tobago united
events.detail: Britain combined two islands with markedly different colonial histories.

events.title: Trinidad and Tobago independent
events.detail: The united colony became a sovereign state.
